dailyRead: This is a wait-for-the-Fed day, and the book is largely frozen into it. The FOMC lands tonight (18:00Z) with CME pricing ~62% hold / ~38% hike - one of the fastest repricings of a meeting in memory, driven by Warsh telling Congress the Committee has no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation. But June NFP was only +57k and headline CPI cooled to 3.5% (core 2.6%), so a hike into a softening labour market would be a genuine shock; the base case is a hawkish hold that sets up September. With no SEP and minimal colour expected, Warsh's tone is the entire dollar trade. Two things already moved before the decision. First, Australia's Q2 CPI printed soft: trimmed mean 3.6% y/y (below the 3.7% consensus, down from 3.7%) with headline easing to 3.8% as fuel dragged - that deflates the RBA Aug-11 hike tail and softens AUD, making AUD/NZD SHORT the cleanest non-Fed trade (NZD's 4.1% Q2 beat is intact). Second, oil BOUNCED - WTI back to ~$81 from Monday's $79 - after Iran launched a surprise attack on US forces that CENTCOM intercepted; the de-escalation is no longer one-way, so USOIL flips from short to RANGE and CAD gets a small reprieve even as its terms-of-trade premium stays gone. UK June CPI at 2.6% (services still 3.6%, two June dissenters) is cooler than the market had assumed, taking some steam out of GBP into BoE Jul 30. Cleanest leans: AUD/NZD SHORT (MED); USD/CAD LONG (MED, Fed-gated, BoC hold at 13:45Z reinforces a parked CAD); NZD/JPY LONG carry (MED); USOIL RANGE; XAU/XAG RANGE pinned to the Fed. The caveat that caps everything: the pause is unsigned and just took a strike - a breakdown re-arms every oil leg in a session.

geopolitics: The de-escalation is no longer clean, and oil is two-way again. After the US paused strikes over the weekend, Iran launched a surprise attack on US forces in the Middle East that CENTCOM says it intercepted - and crude bounced, WTI back to ~$81 from Monday's $79 (Brent ~$87). Talks are contradictory: Trump touts good talks and says Iran asked the US to stop, while Tehran's foreign ministry says there are no current negotiations. Separately, Iran's foreign minister is holding Strait of Hormuz discussions with his Omani and Saudi counterparts, and the strait remains largely closed to commercial traffic (fewer than 10 ships a day versus ~100 normally) - a live bargaining chip. The crucial caveat: the pause is NOT a signed deal and just absorbed a strike, so the marginal headline risk runs both ways. FX transmission: (1) CAD gets a small reprieve from the oil bounce but its terms-of-trade premium is still gone and the BoC holds a sixth time today - USD/CAD LONG stays the cleanest USD leg. (2) The JPY loses a little of its energy relief and stays weakest by spot ~163.7 into BoJ Jul 31. (3) The USD holds a policy bid into the FOMC - DXY long tilt, but Fed-gated. (4) Gold and silver hold a small haven bid (~$4,036 / $57.5) pinned to the Fed - XAU/XAG RANGE. (5) CHF's haven bid is re-armed at the margin. (6) USOIL flips from short to RANGE - the strike restores the premium's two-way risk. Everything oil-linked keys off the same unsigned pause; today it took a hit, so the one-way-down trade is off.
